guarantees: Counted borrowed guards reserve shared task memory, release the authority mutex before returning, and block all four final reclamation boundaries.
Multiple holders, last-release retry, cancellation before/after waiting, pressure refusal/retry, exhaustion and accounting/lock poisoning are covered.
First and genuine successor publication, semantic reads, compiler staging and reopen retain their existing validation.
The catalog adapter borrows a live guard and cannot detach it from its physical publisher.
Three GC wrapper families use the existing shared retirement sink with unchanged journal/receipt order.
limitations: This is in-process staging protection only; no durable task discovery, selected-checkpoint closure, resume, task publication or activation is enabled.
Protection is local to the borrowed publisher and assumes single-writer ownership; it is not a cross-process file lock. Ordinary-engine ownership enforcement remains U2 work.

GC wrappers retain existing pre-barrier journal flushes; refusal prevents final reclamation authority/removal, not every possible journal write. Byte-identical refusal fixtures start with drained journals.
The sweep fixture proves the existing native final callback boundary; its removal authority is a test implementation, not a newly integrated production GC walker.
Caller must retain the guard until checkpoint selection or safe discard, including after dropping the staging adapter; compiler results are not retention capabilities.
No new persisted bytes, capability advertisement, default-v4 cutover, production deployment/service action or retained FS-Server1 database mutation.
